output.summary: An annual or short-lived perennial herb native to the Americas, Mexican tea has irregular branches, long narrow leaves and small green flowers. Its strongly aromatic leaves are used as a vegetable, seasoning and herbal tea, but overdoses of its essential oil have caused deaths.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves, preferably collected before seeding, are used as a vegetable, seasoning and herbal tea; the concentrated essential oil can be fatal.

output.summary: A flowering shrub of northern North America and Greenland, bog Labrador tea grows mainly in cold, acidic wetlands. Its evergreen leaves have leathery, wrinkled tops and densely hairy undersides, while its small white flowers form fragrant clusters. The leaves are brewed as tea, though concentrated doses may be toxic to humans.
output.edibilityNote: Leaves are traditionally brewed as fragrant tea; concentrated doses may be toxic to humans.

output.summary: A large, upright columnar cactus from South America, the Venezuelan apple cactus has grey-green to blue stems with variable spines that may be absent. Its large cream flowers open for one night, and its thornless fruits contain sweetening white flesh and crunchy edible seeds.
output.edibilityNote: The thornless fruit has edible white flesh and small crunchy seeds; the flesh sweetens when the fruit opens fully.

output.summary: A deciduous tree native from China through Southeast Asia to the Indian subcontinent, the orchid tree bears conspicuous pink or white flowers. Its mature pods twist into corkscrews and burst open with an audible clack. In South Asia, its edible buds are cooked in curries, stir-fried or pickled, while flowers and buds make Nepalese pickles.
output.edibilityNote: Buds are cooked in curries, stir-fried or pickled across South Asia; flowers and buds are used in Nepalese pickles.

output.summary: An evergreen flowering perennial native to tropical and southern Africa, the spider plant has long narrow leaves and fleshy, tuberous roots. Its arching flowering stems carry plantlets that droop, touch soil and form roots. The roots are reportedly edible, although preparation is unstated and mild laxative effects are claimed.
output.edibilityNote: Tuberous roots are reportedly edible, with raw or cooked preparation unstated; Nguni people claim mild laxative effects.

output.summary: A hairy perennial shrub from the fynbos of the Cape Peninsula and nearby southwestern Cape, wild mallow grows upright from an underground rootstock and becomes woody at the base. Its crowded, sometimes hood-shaped leaves are fragrant when rubbed, and its flowers range from white to purplish red.

A thorny annual herb native to the Mediterranean Basin, yellow star-thistle begins as a non-spiny leaf rosette before producing stems with yellow, sharply spined flower heads. It commonly occupies disturbed ground and has become invasive in many regions outside its native range.

A succulent flowering plant endemic to the Canary Islands, the candle-plant has jointed branches resembling rows of sausages. Thick elongated leaves cluster at branch tips and fall at the start of the dry season, while fragrant grey-white flowers may appear from March through October.

A hardy flowering perennial native to Croatia's Dalmatian coast, sweet iris grows from a rhizome and bears bluish-green sword-shaped leaves with pale purple to whitish flowers. Oil extracted from its rhizome, called orris root, is used to flavor foods, drinks and gin as well as perfumes.
output.edibilityNote: Orris oil extracted from the rhizome is used to flavor foods, drinks and gin.

output.summary: A herbaceous plant endemic to Mediterranean areas of southwestern Europe, Spanish birthwort occurs from the Iberian Peninsula through southern France to Corsica and Sardinia. It inhabits rocky places, fallows and clearings among heaths, scrub or holm oak groves.
